kinds.label: Android upload keystore

fields.label: Original upload keystore
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Android candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.what: The existing keystore containing the intended private upload key.
fields.why: Candidate signing must use the approved upload key rather than a generated or unrelated identity.
fields.where: Obtain the existing upload-key keystore from its authorized owner; do not generate or reset a key in this guide. Future native capture accepts an original owner-private file outside the selected project. A permission or physical-exclusion refusal preserves the original; it is not permission to chmod, move or delete it.
fields.format: Nonempty original .jks, .keystore, .p12 or .pfx; at most 32 MiB. Suffixes are selection hints, not proof. JKS header or supported PFX envelope recognition would remain limited.
fields.failure: Import is unavailable. A later unsupported format, changed source, size or permission refusal is not a native password/key verdict. Originals are preserved.

fields.label: Keystore password
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Android candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.what: The password protecting the keystore container.
fields.why: The store password and private-key password may differ.
fields.where: Use the password held by the authorized keystore owner, not a Google account password.
fields.format: The original nonempty, NUL-free value, with no trimming or normalization. Future input is write-only; never put it in project configuration, command arguments or logs.
fields.failure: A missing password is a missing companion field, not a failed password test. No password is entered or tested here.

fields.label: Private-key alias
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Android candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.what: The selected private-key entry name within the keystore.
fields.why: A file can contain other entries; an alias string alone does not establish an intended private key.
fields.where: Ask the authorized key owner for the exact existing upload-key alias.
fields.format: 1-255 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots or hyphens. Preserve exact spelling. The core owns the format rule; no alias lookup is performed.
fields.failure: A missing/ill-formed alias blocks later applicable use. A well-formed alias remains unverified for entry existence or key type.

fields.label: Private-key password
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Android candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.what: The password for the selected private-key entry.
fields.why: An accessible keystore does not prove that its intended private key can be used.
fields.where: Use the selected entry password held by the authorized owner; it may differ from the keystore password.
fields.format: The original nonempty, NUL-free value, with no trimming or normalization. Future input is write-only; never put it in project configuration, command arguments or logs.
fields.failure: Missing input is not a password failure. Native signing/password validation remains unavailable and not run.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: recognize a supported JKS header or a bounded PFX envelope.
notVerified: PrivateKeyEntry, key usability, validity and approved upload fingerprint

kinds.label: Android Firebase client document

fields.label: Original google-services.json
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Android candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose. Additionally services.androidFirebase must be required.
fields.what: The Firebase client configuration for the intended Android application.
fields.why: Every Android client must have the expected decoded shape, with at least one exact configured applicationId match.
fields.where: Download the client document for this Android app from Firebase Project Settings. Do not substitute an exported service-account private key. Future native capture accepts an original owner-private file outside the selected project. A permission or physical-exclusion refusal preserves the original; it is not permission to chmod, move or delete it.
fields.format: Nonempty UTF-8 JSON .json, at most 4 MiB. Planned desktop limits/duplicate refusal do not change existing CLI parsing.
fields.failure: An inapplicable document is not a requirement. Later malformed clients or an identity mismatch prevent matching-document acceptance; no Firebase service is contacted here.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: bounded client-document shape and exact configured applicationId match.
notVerified: API permissions, authorization and live service availability

kinds.label: Apple Distribution identity

fields.label: Original Distribution P12
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects iOS candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.what: An exported Apple Distribution certificate and private-key container.
fields.why: A P12 signing identity is different authority from an App Store Connect P8 API key.
fields.where: Obtain the approved exported identity from its authorized owner; this guide does not install it in a signing keychain. Future native capture accepts an original owner-private file outside the selected project. A permission or physical-exclusion refusal preserves the original; it is not permission to chmod, move or delete it.
fields.format: Nonempty original .p12 or .pfx, at most 32 MiB. Planned supported PFX envelope recognition does not decrypt or verify its contents.
fields.failure: Malformed/unsupported envelope or source refusal preserves the original. A saved envelope would still not establish a correct password, private key or Distribution identity.

fields.label: P12 export password
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects iOS candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.what: The private password used when exporting this P12.
fields.why: The export password is a companion to this exact identity, not the Apple account password.
fields.where: Use the existing export password from the authorized identity owner.
fields.format: The original nonempty, NUL-free value, with no trimming or normalization. Future input is write-only; never put it in project configuration, command arguments or logs.
fields.failure: Missing companion input is missing, not a rejected password. No decryption, key installation or password test occurs here.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: recognize the supported PFX version/content envelope.
notVerified: Certificate/key match, chain, validity and approved Distribution identity

kinds.label: Apple provisioning profile

fields.label: Original App Store provisioning profile
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects iOS candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose.
fields.why: Signing requires the approved team, app, entitlements and signer to agree; embedded claims alone are not trusted.
fields.where: Obtain the intended App Store distribution profile from the authorized Apple developer team. Future native capture accepts an original owner-private file outside the selected project. A permission or physical-exclusion refusal preserves the original; it is not permission to chmod, move or delete it.
fields.format: Nonempty original .mobileprovision, at most 4 MiB. Planned bounded supported CMS SignedData envelope parsing does not accept a bare plist as an authenticated profile.
fields.failure: A malformed or unsupported container cannot be treated as a profile. No Apple signature/trust, expiry, team or entitlement check is performed here.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: recognize a bounded supported CMS SignedData envelope.
notVerified: Team, bundle ID, entitlement and certificate/profile relationships

kinds.label: App Store Connect API key

fields.label: Original App Store Connect P8
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects App Store Connect authority for the chosen iOS stage and purpose, not merely because an iOS build is selected.
fields.what: The unencrypted PKCS#8 API private key issued for App Store Connect access.
fields.why: This is Store account authority, not an Apple Distribution P12 signing identity.
fields.where: Obtain the original downloaded API key from the authorized App Store Connect account owner. Do not place it in the repository. Future native capture accepts an original owner-private file outside the selected project. A permission or physical-exclusion refusal preserves the original; it is not permission to chmod, move or delete it.
fields.format: Nonempty original .p8, at most 4 MiB. Planned unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM/DER envelope plus EC/P-256 identifiers only; encrypted or unsupported variants remain unavailable.
fields.failure: A recognized envelope does not prove mathematical key validity, ownership, revocation state or permissions. No Store request occurs here.

fields.label: App Store Connect key ID
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects App Store Connect authority for the chosen iOS stage and purpose, not merely because an iOS build is selected.
fields.what: The public identifier assigned to this exact API key.
fields.why: The later Store client must pair the intended key and issuer; matching text is not proof of access.
fields.where: Read the key ID for this key in App Store Connect API key administration.
fields.format: Exactly 10 uppercase ASCII letters or digits; the core owns this format rule. This guide neither accepts nor echoes a supplied identifier.
fields.failure: Missing or ill-formed input is a missing/format issue, not failed account authentication.

fields.label: App Store Connect issuer ID
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects App Store Connect authority for the chosen iOS stage and purpose, not merely because an iOS build is selected.
fields.what: The issuer identifier for the account that owns the API key.
fields.why: A syntactically valid UUID does not prove the selected account owns or accepts the key.
fields.where: Read the issuer ID from the authorized account API key administration.
fields.format: UUID spelling: 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal characters, with hyphens; preserve the intended issuer.
fields.failure: Missing or ill-formed input blocks applicable later use. Account identity and Store authorization stay unverified.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: recognize unencrypted PKCS#8 with EC/P-256 envelope identifiers.
Planned only, not run: shared scalar key-ID/issuer-ID format rules.
notVerified: Mathematical private-key validity and account ownership
Revocation and App Store Connect permissions

kinds.label: iOS Firebase client document

fields.label: Original GoogleService-Info.plist
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects iOS candidate signing for the current project, stage and purpose. Additionally services.iosFirebase must be required.
fields.what: The Firebase client plist for the configured iOS app.
fields.why: The decoded top-level BUNDLE_ID string must exactly equal the configured bundleId.
fields.where: Download the intended iOS app client file from Firebase Project Settings. It is not a provisioning profile or an exported service private key. Future native capture accepts an original owner-private file outside the selected project. A permission or physical-exclusion refusal preserves the original; it is not permission to chmod, move or delete it.
fields.format: Nonempty original .plist, at most 4 MiB. Future supported binary/XML parsing needs explicit capacity, duplicate and entity controls; those variants are not yet enabled.
fields.failure: Malformed, unsupported or mismatched documents cannot claim matching-app format validity. Permission/size refusals preserve the original and no Firebase service is contacted.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: bounded supported plist dictionary and exact string BUNDLE_ID match.

kinds.label: Google workload identity federation

fields.label: Workload identity provider
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Google Store authority for the chosen Android stage and purpose; local CLI ADC substitution remains a separate existing CLI path.
fields.what: The Google workload identity provider assigned to the protected workflow.
fields.why: Federation avoids exporting a reusable service-account private key; the provider must still be configured and authorized.
fields.where: Ask the cloud administrator for the reviewed provider bound to this repository and protected workflow.
fields.format: projects/NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER; a positive decimal project number without a leading zero and allowed pool/provider identifier characters.
fields.failure: Syntax cannot prove provider existence, repository binding or token exchange. This guide does not log in, request OIDC or import Google ADC.

fields.label: Federated service-account email
fields.requiredWhen: When the shared core selects Google Store authority for the chosen Android stage and purpose; local CLI ADC substitution remains a separate existing CLI path.
fields.what: The least-privileged Google service account to impersonate.
fields.why: Federation and intended Play roles must both be configured; an email grants no authority by itself.
fields.where: Obtain the exact authorized service-account email from the cloud/Play administrator.
fields.format: A service-account email ending in .iam.gserviceaccount.com, subject to the shared core identifier rule. Never paste a service-account JSON private key.
fields.failure: Missing/ill-formed configuration is distinct from denied federation or Play access. Both native/service checks are not run.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: shared provider-path and service-account identifier format rules.
notVerified: Provider existence, repository binding and successful federation
Local CLI ADC validity; ADC import is deferred

kinds.label: Private project dependency access

fields.label: Read-only project token
fields.requiredWhen: When source.projectReadTokenRequired is true and the shared core selects candidate full/signing requirements; it is a project requirement, not a Store credential.
fields.what: An explicitly authorized read-only token for private project dependencies.
fields.why: Only the required source dependency scope should be granted; do not reuse Store or administrator credentials.
fields.where: Obtain a narrowly scoped read-only dependency token through the project owner's approved access process.
fields.format: The original nonempty, NUL-free value, with no trimming or normalization. Future input is write-only; never put it in project configuration, command arguments or logs.
fields.failure: Missing input matters only when selected by core requirements. This guide performs no source fetch, token request or permission check.

plannedChecks: Planned only, not run: bounded presence/value admission in the separately reviewed future credential flow.
notVerified: Revocation, expiry and any successful source fetch

controls.label: Selected project
controls.requiredWhen: For later context-specific preparation or assignment.
controls.what: The current registered project and core-validated draft.
controls.why: An app-wide library entry must not silently become authority for another project.
controls.where: Use the existing selected project and configuration workflow, not a credential filename or repository guess.
controls.format: Future bindings use the actual native project/document lifetime and approved draft; project IDs are session-local.
controls.failure: No assignment is performed here. Project/draft changes invalidate later dependent observations rather than proving failure.

controls.label: Selected platform
controls.requiredWhen: For later applicable platform-specific use; the project-token rule remains core-owned.
controls.what: The enabled Android or iOS selection within the current project context.
controls.why: Broad catalogue visibility must not satisfy a disabled or unrelated platform requirement.
controls.where: Use the platform selection associated with the core-validated draft.
controls.format: This static guide lists kinds but does not choose platforms or make requirements applicable.
controls.failure: An inapplicable selection is not invalid credential material and grants no other platform authority.

controls.label: Release stage
controls.what: Candidate, external-testing or production as selected by the shared core.
controls.why: Candidate signing and later Store authority have different requirements.
controls.where: Use the selected release stage in the reviewed project workflow.
controls.format: Static catalogue visibility across stages is not assignment permission.
controls.failure: Changing stage makes prior context-bound observations stale; no release flow is enabled here.

controls.label: Credential purpose
controls.requiredWhen: For later context-bound full, signing or Store use.
controls.what: The narrow purpose selected by the shared requirement policy.
controls.why: A Store API credential is not automatically a build-signing credential.
controls.where: Use the existing workflow purpose; React does not reproduce the selector.
controls.format: Core requirements preserve full/signing/store and existing SKIP/MANUAL distinctions.
controls.failure: An inapplicable kind cannot satisfy another purpose. No native or Store operation runs here.

controls.label: Storage mode
controls.requiredWhen: Only when an implemented future flow requests explicit storage consent.
controls.what: Choose authenticated encrypted persistence or separately consented session-only memory.
controls.why: Failed or inaccessible persistence must never silently become a session save.
controls.where: A future supported native credential flow will state the actual available backend; this guide has no mode input.
controls.format: Persistent mode requires a qualified OS keyring; session-only is bounded memory, never a plaintext disk fallback.
controls.failure: Locked, denied, unavailable, missing-key and unknown completion are distinct. Do not recreate an inaccessible key or claim persistence.

controls.label: Private library label
controls.requiredWhen: Only for a future saved entry; use the fixed nonsecret kind label by default.
controls.what: A user-facing description of the intended material, not a secret identifier.
controls.why: Filenames and user labels can contain private information; a label is not identity or verification.
controls.where: Use a short nonsecret description; never autofill it from a filename, account key ID or secret.
controls.format: The planned label bound is 128 UTF-8 bytes. Labels are encrypted in persistent descriptors; no entry can be saved here.
controls.failure: A label does not rename, move or change the original. Do not put passwords or tokens in labels.

controls.label: Choose original file
controls.requiredWhen: Only for a supported file kind in a future native capture flow.
controls.what: Select one original private file for bounded native capture.
controls.why: Renderer paths, suffixes and prior pathname checks are not custody of the original bytes.
controls.where: Use the future native picker, never paste a path/Base64 into React or place assets manually in a vault directory.
controls.format: The supported source must be owner-private and physically outside the selected project; capture preserves the original.
controls.failure: Permission, overlap, unsupported variant or changed-source refusal preserves the original. Do not advise chmod, move or delete to bypass refusal.

controls.label: Prepare credential
controls.requiredWhen: After future original capture and required companion entry for the displayed context.
controls.what: A bounded pure assessment of the captured format observations and supplied companion fields.
controls.why: Presence and mechanical shape need their own honest limits before a save can be reviewed.
controls.where: Only a separately reviewed native command can combine captured-byte facts with core assessment.
controls.format: This guide accepts no secret values or file observations. Missing companions are missing, not failed passwords.
controls.failure: Invalid/stale/inapplicable observations cannot authorize a save; no signing/native/service check is implied.

controls.label: Review proposed copy
controls.requiredWhen: Before any future save, replacement or deletion is admitted.
controls.what: Confirm the exact context, kind, limited checks and intended action.
controls.why: A preview is finite and must not be reused after draft, document or revision changes.
controls.where: Use the future review panel bound to the actual original native document.
controls.format: All controls need visible labels, keyboard operation and an explicit pending state. Secret values stay write-only with no reveal/readback.
controls.failure: Document loss or stale preview prevents a not-yet-admitted commit. This static screen issues no token or authority.

controls.label: Save or keep for session
controls.requiredWhen: Only after future explicit review and supported-mode consent.
controls.what: Save an encrypted copy or keep one bounded session-only entry.
controls.why: Stored material is not an assignment, successful password test or release-ready credential.
controls.where: The private library is outside projects; do not copy into the repository, environment, clipboard export or plaintext staging.
controls.format: A future save uses one single-use preview. Persistent success requires authenticated publication, durability and settled cleanup.
controls.failure: A failed or cancelled replacement can preserve old stored bytes, but affected assignments stay unavailable until explicit successful preparation and assignment. Unknown cleanup must be reported; there is no silent mode fallback. This reference guide itself performs no save.

controls.label: Assign to current context
controls.requiredWhen: When a future workflow explicitly binds a known entry revision to selected core requirements.
controls.why: Library presence must not imply automatic discovery or use across projects or sessions.
controls.where: Review the displayed current context and exact entry revision in the future assignment flow.
controls.format: A new session requires reassignment. Rebinding re-assesses applicable format/identity without exporting or invoking a consumer.
controls.failure: Wrong context, stale revision, locked or unavailable payload cannot be used. Assignment is not native or online verification.

controls.label: Replace library entry
controls.requiredWhen: Only after a future explicit preview of the known entry and expected revision.
controls.what: Create a fresh revision of the same credential kind.
controls.why: Existing assignments cannot stay usable while a replacement may have taken effect.
controls.where: Select the known private-library entry, never infer replacement from a filename or label.
controls.format: Affected assignments become unavailable by admission; only positive known-safe revalidation can restore an old revision.
controls.failure: Ambiguous publication/durability/cleanup pauses mutation; no blind retry or rollback. The original source and unrelated records remain untouched.

controls.label: Delete library entry
controls.requiredWhen: Only after a future explicit preview of the known record/revision.
controls.what: Remove the selected private-library record, not the original file or wrapping key.
controls.why: A pending or uncertain removal must not leave its assignments usable.
controls.where: Confirm the exact library entry in the future delete review.
controls.format: Deletion is not secure SSD/snapshot erasure, account revocation or master-key rotation.
controls.failure: Assignments stay unavailable on unknown effects. Never delete unrelated records or assume an error proves no effect.

controls.label: Cancel pending interaction
controls.requiredWhen: While a future picker, prompt, preparation or not-yet-admitted action is pending.
controls.what: Request cancellation without abandoning original native work.
controls.why: A blocked native prompt or admitted commit can outlive the invoking UI.
controls.where: Use a labelled keyboard-accessible cancel control and visible waiting/pending state.
controls.format: Cancellation may latch until the native call returns; timeout is not rollback or proof of safe exit.
controls.failure: An admitted finite commit must settle its publication/cleanup. Busy or cleanup-unknown stays explicit rather than claiming successful cancellation.

controls.label: Discard unsaved preparation
controls.requiredWhen: For a future pending selection/preview or explicit session-only discard.
controls.what: Invalidate unused selection/preview authority and release owned private buffers.
controls.why: An old preview must not be replayed or used by a new document.
controls.where: Use explicit discard; session-only data loss requires truthful confirmation.
controls.format: Best-effort owned-memory wiping does not erase every JS/OS/SDK/clipboard copy. Originals and existing persistent records are preserved.
controls.failure: Do not abandon a native operation or report safe cleanup until its owned lifetime settles. No discard action is enabled here.

controls.label: Lock private library
controls.requiredWhen: When a future unlocked library/session must become unavailable.
controls.what: Invalidate future-use authority and drop owned private buffers after pending work settles.
controls.why: Unlocked/stored state is distinct from assigned or verified credentials.
controls.where: Use an explicit lock/discard-session action with clear confirmation and pending guidance.
controls.format: No wrapping-key reset, export, import or rotation is included. AEAD does not prevent older valid-backup rollback or an already compromised host.
controls.failure: Lock is not key revocation or perfect memory/disk erasure. Unknown native cleanup remains pending and must not be hidden.

states.label: Unknown
states.meaning: No sufficient current observation has been made. The static guide and catalogue never report a private input as read.

states.label: Missing requirement
states.meaning: The core selected a requirement but its future required input/companion is absent. This is not a failed password or native test.

states.label: Invalid within a named check
states.meaning: A supported, actually performed finite check found a format/value problem. State the precise check; unsupported, stale or unknown is not invalid.

states.label: Configured, not verified
states.meaning: Material or companion values are present with only the stated header/envelope/scalar scope. Presence is not proof of signing or Store usability.

states.label: Limited format-valid scope
states.meaning: Only an actually checked bounded matching Firebase client document may claim its named shape/application-identity scope. Not native or service validity.

states.label: Native checks not run
states.meaning: No keytool/OpenSSL/security, password, key/certificate/profile validation, signing installation or native consumer was executed.

states.label: Service checks not run
states.meaning: No account authentication, OIDC exchange, Firebase/Play/App Store request or permission verification was performed.

states.label: Stored copy
states.meaning: A future confirmed encrypted/session-only library copy exists. Storage alone is not payload validation, assignment, release readiness or persistent portability.

states.label: Locked or inaccessible
states.meaning: Private payloads are unavailable. Locked, denied, unsupported, missing-key and uncertain outcomes must remain distinct; no replacement key is silently created.

states.label: Unlocked this session
states.meaning: A future explicit open obtained current access. It does not prove every payload is authenticated or any signing credential is usable.

states.label: Assigned for this context
states.meaning: A future known entry revision is bound in memory to the displayed current context. A new session, mutation or relevant context change requires revalidation/reassignment.

states.label: Stale observation or assignment
states.meaning: The project/draft/platform/stage/purpose/policy or entry revision changed. Previous facts no longer authorize use; this is neither invalidity nor verification.

states.label: Cleanup or durability unknown
states.meaning: An operation may have affected storage without confirmed durability/cleanup. Affected assignments remain unavailable and mutations pause; no automatic retry/rollback.

states.label: Unavailable in this build
states.meaning: This guide-only slice has no credential inputs, picker, vault, assignment, authentication, verification or Store action. Future target/backend support requires separate qualification.
